title: Exact finite-free descent and ordinary normalized balancing
statement: Let C be a category in Type (u+1) with hom universe u, essentially small in u+1, let J be any Grothendieck topology on C, and let A and B be commutative rings in Type (u+1) with an A-algebra structure. Let r be a natural number and basis a basis of B over A indexed by Fin r. There exists a FiniteFreeScalarTensorCalculus J r basis [def-sf-finite-free-scalar-calculus-data]: exact scalar extension and restriction, universal exact derived descent, the normalized derived scalar adjunction, conservative derived restriction, the normalized finite-basis decomposition, preservation of K-flatness, and the two normalized ordinary sheaf balancing maps. No finiteness of the rings, scheme hypotheses, derived tensor comparison, constructibility or Tor interval is assumed or concluded.

proof.text:
Write $E(M)=M\otimes_{A_W}B_W$ for ordinary extension. The basis identifies $B_W$ with $A_W^{\oplus r}$: the basis and its coordinate maps on constant presheaves sheafify to mutually inverse module maps. The sheaf-tensor definition then gives inverse natural maps
$$M^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow UE(M),\quad(m_j)\longmapsto\sum_jm_j\otimes b_j,\qquad m\otimes\sum_ja_jb_j\longmapsto(a_jm)_j.$$
These formulas are checked on local pure tensors and therefore after sheafification. Restriction leaves underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. By the cited kernel/cokernel descriptions it is exact and reflects exact sequences; a module map with invertible underlying additive map has a linear inverse. Finite sums of exact sequences are exact, component by component, so the displayed basis identification makes $E$ exact as well. This includes $r=0$; no faithfulness of $E$ is claimed.

source.place: Tag 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), preceding change-of-rings construction; elementary basis calculation

proof.text: Exact-functor descent supplies $D(E)$ and $D(U)$, represented termwise on every complex. Exact-functor homology gives $H^q(EC)=E H^q(C)$ and $H^q(UC)=U H^q(C)$. For a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$, exactness makes $EP\to EC$ a quasi-isomorphism. The K-flat computation of derived change of rings identifies $TP$ and $TC$ with $EP$; hence $D(E)\cong T$ canonically, using these resolution maps. This comparison is natural and independent of resolution by the canonical-comparison clause of derived change of rings. Localizing the basis maps of step 1 gives $UTK\cong K^{\oplus r}$; its $j$th inclusion is the localized map $p\mapsto p\otimes b_j$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); exact-functor descent and finite-free basis

proof.text: On sheaves the mutually inverse adjunction formulas are $f\mapsto(m\mapsto f(m\otimes1))$ and $g\mapsto(m\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(m))$. Balancedness makes the latter well defined, and both formulas commute with restriction and sheafification. Thus the unit is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and the counit is $n\otimes b\mapsto bn$. The same degreewise formulas commute with differentials and satisfy the triangle identities, since both triangle composites send each local generator to itself. Apply the adjunction-localization theorem to these functors on cochain complexes and the two quasi-isomorphism localizations; the exact functors of step 2 provide its required factorization isomorphisms. Its unit/counit formulas give $D(E)\dashv D(U)$ with the localized scalar unit and counit. Transport through the canonical $D(E)\cong T$ gives precisely $T\dashv U$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict); localization via lem-sfb-adjunction-localization, including its unit and counit formulas

proof.text: For a derived morphism $v$, the cohomology comparison of step 2 identifies $H^q(Uv)$ with $U H^q(v)$. If $Uv$ is invertible, restriction reflects invertibility on sheaves by step 1, so every $H^q(v)$ is invertible. The cohomology criterion for unbounded derived isomorphisms implies that $v$ is invertible. Applying this to $0\to N$ also shows that $UN=0$ implies $N=0$. In particular $U$ reflects each individual cohomology vanishing, since its value on a sheaf has the same underlying abelian sheaf.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), together with exact restriction and the cohomology criterion

proof.text: The cited K-flat change-of-rings theorem applies to the identity underlying topos with ring map $A_W\to B_W$, on either of the chosen small sites. It says that $EP$ is K-flat over $B_W$ for every K-flat $A_W$-complex $P$, without any assumption on its individual terms. For the flat-term resolutions used below, the ringed-pullback theorem additionally says that $EP$ has flat terms.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); the existing all-independent change-of-rings lemma removes the termwise-flatness requirement for K-flatness itself

proof.text: For the ordinary tensor comparison, sheafify the balanced maps (b tensor m) tensor n ↦ m tensor bn and m tensor n ↦ (1 tensor m) tensor n. The balancing relations make the composites identities. Their images under the two sheafification units are precisely the local pure-tensor formulas; this supplies sheaf_balance, balance_forward and balance_inverse. No derived tensor or constructibility conclusion is asserted.
